primitives.verbatim_quote: 242 RISK, UNCERTAINTY, AND PROFIT is the variation in the power of reading human nature, of forecasting the conduct of other men, as contrasted with scientific judgment in regard to natural phenomena.
primitives.assumptions: Human behavior varies more than natural phenomena; judgment quality is subjective.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When predictive models fail due to non-stationary human behavior.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that risk, uncertainty, and profit are not merely statistical constructs but reflect the variability in human judgment and behavior. The first primitive, Risk-Uncertainty-Profit Variation, establishes a foundational distinction between human judgment and natural phenomena. This variation is not just about prediction accuracy but about the subjective capacity to read and anticipate human behavior. The second primitive, Judgment-Execution Capacity, introduces a dualism: one can judge well but fail to execute, or vice versa. This duality implies a bifurcation in decision-making systems—where cognitive and operational capabilities diverge. The third primitive, Conative Attitude Toward Uncertainty, adds a motivational layer: individuals do not simply assess uncertainty but react to it with varying degrees of risk-seeking or risk-averse behavior. These three primitives form a triadic structure where each element interacts with the others. For instance, high judgment capacity without strong execution leads to paralysis; low confidence but high conative attitude may lead to reckless action. The failure mode occurs when these dimensions are misaligned—such as when overconfidence in judgment leads to poor execution, or when aversion to uncertainty blocks adaptive responses. The epistemic structure thus reflects a layered cognitive architecture: perception (judgment), action (execution), and motivation (attitude). Each layer has its own variability and interaction dynamics, forming a multi-dimensional space of decision-making behavior.
